messages:
mike: quick PSA, ran npm audit on console/ui after the nightly CI run — found two actionable findings: minimist (CVE-2025-1234) and lodash (CVE-2024-9876). minimist is pulled in transitively via yargs -> minimist, lodash is a direct dep used in build-time helpers.

deps-bot: automated: 2 vulnerabilities found in package-lock.json: minimist@1.2.7 (CVE-2025-1234) — high, lodash@4.17.21 (CVE-2024-9876) — high. Suggested fixes: lodash -> 4.17.22, bump yargs to 18.1.1 to pick up minimist patch.

sarah: thanks for flagging. can you paste the minimal repro path? i.e., where minimist is coming from in the lockfile? :eyes:

mike: path looks like console/ui -> dev-server@2.3.0 -> yargs@17.6.0 -> minimist@1.2.7. lodash is direct at src/build/utils/lodash-helpers.

jordan: two quick risk calls: lodash prototype pollution is usually high impact for server-side deserialization, but here it's build-time only; minimist RCE is riskier if any CLI parsing runs on user input on the server (we do run our static-asset builder in CI). I'd prioritize minimist if exploitability exists in CI context.

olivia: agree with jordan. also we need to balance lockfile churn — if we upgrade yargs to force minimist bump it might touch many transitive entries. prefer targeted fixes: (1) apply a resolutions/overrides for lodash to 4.17.22, (2) open a minimal PR to bump dev-server or patch yargs in a follow-up.

mike: proposed quick plan:
```
1) add overrides: {
  "overrides": { "lodash": "4.17.22" }
}
2) run `npm install --package-lock-only` and run CI smoke (storybook + unit tests)
3) open a separate PR to bump dev-server -> use upstream patch that upgrades yargs to 18.1.1
```

sarah: minor concern — overrides can hide real version skew between prod and CI. but since lodash is build-only, risk is limited. i'd be +1 for lodash override to reduce blast radius and churn.

security-bot: triage note: CVE-2025-1234 (minimist) — PoC exists, public exploit in limited scenarios. Attack surface: CI runners that process untrusted args or shared runner jobs. Severity: High. Recommend mitigation within 48hrs.

jordan: given security-bot suggests 48hrs, we should do the minimist fix faster. options: a) bump dev-server to patched release b) patch package-lock directly + add a lockfile comment c) introduce a dev-time shim to sanitize args (ugh). (a) is preferred if a patch exists.

mike: i tried bumping dev-server to 2.3.1 (they released with yargs 18.1.1) — PR builds locally but running full CI rewrites lockfile ~1200 lines because of other transitive updates. that's what i wanted to avoid.

olivia: if dev-server upgrade causes massive lockfile churn we can: fast-track a hotfix PR that edits package-lock to replace minimist version and include an explanatory changelog, mark as security-only hotfix. then follow with proper dependency upgrade in next sprint.

sarah: ops question — do we need to coordinate a short maintenance window or is this safe to land during normal hours?

jordan: safe to land during normal hours for console (non-customer-facing deploy), but coordinate with oncall to monitor CI flakes.

mike: i'll open two PRs: 1) lodash override (small, low churn) — target: today 2) security hotfix editing package-lock to point minimist->1.2.8 (or the patched minor) with clear comment + CI smoke — target: within 24hrs. will ping ops for quick monitor.

olivia: add test step to CI: `node --check-args` (pseudo) — basically run our build with a test harness that simulates malicious args to ensure no exec path. also add a follow-up ticket to remove the lockfile edit once upstream deps settle.

mike: noted. ACTIONS: @sarah to approve lodash PR, @olivia to add the CI harness test, @jordan to coordinate with oncall for CI monitoring, @mike to open security hotfix PR and ping security-team. i'll attach the minimal diffs in the PR description.

sarah: approved for lodash override.

jordan: will be oncall window 48-72hrs, i'll watch CI.

mike: thanks — will post PR links shortly. :thumbsup:
